questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in cell E2 that computes the total price by multiplying the *Quantity* by the *Unit Price* for each item which is found in the Item sheet. Use the hint below to complete the formula.

```
=IF(C2="S1",D2*Item!C$2,....
```

(In the hint, the sign `$` before the row number makes that row number absolute.)

Write down the formula in cell E2 in the line below. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the hint: in the General sheet, **C2** holds the item code (S1, S2...), **D2** the quantity, and in the **Item** sheet the unit price of the first item is in **C2** (the column of unit prices is C, one item per row from row 2). The total price of a row is the quantity multiplied by the unit price of the item whose code is in column C, so each item code needs its own test. With n item codes S1, S2, ..., Sn listed in rows 2 to n+1 of the Item sheet, the formula in **E2** is a nested IF:

```
=IF(C2="S1",D2*Item!C$2,IF(C2="S2",D2*Item!C$3,IF(C2="S3",D2*Item!C$4, ... ,D2*Item!C$(n+1))))
```

The last IF has no further test: the final value is the product for the last code Sn. For example, if the Item sheet lists three items S1, S2, S3 in rows 2, 3 and 4:

```
=IF(C2="S1",D2*Item!C$2,IF(C2="S2",D2*Item!C$3,D2*Item!C$4))
```

Press Enter, then copy the formula down to **E21** (drag the fill handle or double-click it). The row number is anchored in `Item!C$2` (dollar sign before the row number only), so that the references C2 and D2 move down with each row while the reference to the Item sheet row of each code does not depend on the row where the formula is copied.

An equivalent shorter formula, valid whatever the number of items, uses a lookup (the Item sheet columns being ItemCode, ItemName, UnitPrice in A, B, C). With the three items above:

```
=D2*VLOOKUP(C2,Item!$A$2:$C$4,3,FALSE)
```

Check with invented data (items S1, S2, S3 at 150, 500 and 4000): the nested IF and VLOOKUP give the same results, for example 20 units of S1 give 20 x 150 = 3000 and 44 units of S3 give 44 x 4000 = 176000. The question asks for the nested IF built from the hint, so write that one.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the totals along row 22 in the D and E columns.
Write down the formula in cell E22 in the line below. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The data are in rows 2 to 21, so the totals go in row 22:

```
D22:  =SUM(D2:D21)
E22:  =SUM(E2:E21)
```

The formula in cell **E22** is `=SUM(E2:E21)`. The *AutoSum* button (*Home* > *Editing* > Sigma) generates the same formula; the cell D22 is filled in the same way, or by copying E22 to D22 (the references adjust to D2:D21). Do not include row 22 itself in the range, otherwise Excel reports a circular reference.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a vertical bar chart of *Item Code* against *Total Price*. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the *Item Code* column and the *Total Price* column without the totals row: click C1, drag to C21, then hold Ctrl and select E1:E21 (the headings are included so that the series is named). *Insert* > *Charts* > *Column* > **Clustered Column** (a vertical bar chart). One bar is drawn for each row of the table, labelled with its item code on the horizontal axis and with its total price on the vertical axis. Do not include row 22 (the totals): the TOTAL bar would dwarf all the others.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Set the title of chart to *Sales*; name the horizontal axis as *Item Code* and vertical axis as *Total Price*. Move the bar chart to the area just below the table so that it prints on the same page as the table.

**Save the workbook and print the *GeneralSheet* sheet only.** *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Title.** Select the chart, *Chart Design* > *Add Chart Element* > *Chart Title* > *Above Chart*, and type **Sales**.
2. **Axis titles.** *Add Chart Element* > *Axis Titles* > *Primary Horizontal*: type **Item Code**; *Primary Vertical*: type **Total Price**.
3. **Position.** Drag the chart (by its border) to the free area just below the table, with its top-left corner at about cell A24, so that it does not cover the table (rows 1 to 22) and stays within the page width.
4. **Save** the workbook (Ctrl+S) in the candidate folder, keeping the name OnlineSales.
5. **Print.** Select the sheet tab of the sheet that holds the table and the chart (the paper writes *GeneralSheet*; the sheet is called *General* in question 1 of this task), then *File* > *Print* > *Print Active Sheets*, and check in *Print Preview* that the table and the chart are on one page (use *Page Layout* > *Fit to 1 page* if the chart is cut off). Staple the printout in the booklet.

Marking guide (3 marks): chart title (1), the two axis titles (1), chart placed below the table and printed on the same page, with only that sheet printed (1).
